task: DEEP WEB RESEARCH: ASUS ExpertBook P1 (P1503CVA) Ubuntu 26.04.1 provisioning — close all remaining gaps after a major methodology shift. Context: We discovered the Ubuntu 26.04.1 desktop ISO has a MODERN GPT layout with a SEPARATE 5MB embedded EFI System Partition (partition 2), which means the classic 'dd creates unpatchable read-only ISO9660' warning is OUTDATED for this ISO — dd IS viable because the ESP remains a writable FAT32 partition that can be patched with the dual-signed shim. This invalidates part of our existing runbook. Research all remaining gaps with authoritative sources (Ubuntu docs, AskUbuntu, ASUS support, Leo Gaggl blog, kernel docs): (1) Verify dd vs usb-creator-gtk for Ubuntu 24.04+/26.04 ISOs — confirm the separate-ESP layout makes dd+shim-patch valid; cite sources. (2) Verify the dual-signed shim fix mechanism — is /usr/lib/shim/shimx64.efi.dualsigned still the correct file (signed by both Canonical + Microsoft UEFI CA)? Any changes in shim 15.8+/16? (3) Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS specifics — confirm release exists, what's new, known installer/boot issues. (4) ASUS ExpertBook P1 (P1503CVA) Secure Boot specifics — dual-signed shim on this model, BIOS version considerations, F2 boot menu, known Ubuntu issues (Wi-Fi chipset, audio, etc). (5) i7-13620H Raptor Lake-H on Ubuntu 26.04 — P-core/E-core scheduling, known kernel issues, AVX-VNNI confirmation. (6) DDR5-5200 32GB upgrade (2x16GB) — ExpertBook P1 compatibility, recommended kits. (7) 2230 NVMe options for Slot 2 — current best drives (WD SN740, Samsung PM991a, etc), availability 2026. (8) Ventoy vs dd+shim — since the USB already had Ventoy, is Ventoy+shim patch a better alternative? Compare approaches. Deliver: structured research report with sources cited, confidence levels, and any corrections to our existing runbook assumptions.
context: From roc_racoon (Sovereign Miner / hardware specialist). Major methodology shift: the runbook at ../ASUS-ExpertBook-P1-boot-drive--and-NVMe-guide.md warned against dd because it assumed the EFI was embedded inside ISO9660 (unpatchable). We verified with fdisk that the Ubuntu 26.04.1 ISO has GPT layout: partition 1 = 6GB ISO9660 data, partition 2 = 5MB EFI System (FAT32, writable), partition 3 = 300K. This means dd + mount sdb2 + replace bootx64.efi with shimx64.efi.dualsigned is valid. Need authoritative confirmation and all remaining gap closure before burning the USB. Priority: HIGH.
